title: Eichler Home Exterior Repair: T1-11 Siding, Flat Roof, and Post-Beam Dry Rot on the Peninsula
metaTitle: Eichler Home Repair: T1-11 Siding, Flat Roof, Dry Rot (Peninsula 2026)
excerpt: Eichlers are architectural icons — and maintenance headaches. Here's how to repair T1-11 siding, flat roofs, and post-and-beam framing on Peninsula and San Jose Eichlers without destroying what makes them Eichlers.

outline.h2: The Short Answer: Eichlers Age Predictably. Here's the Repair Playbook.
outline.notes: Eichlers (built 1949-1974) have three chronic exterior problems: T1-11 siding failure at grade and around windows, flat/low-slope roof failure at year 15-25, and post-and-beam dry rot where wood meets concrete slab. Total exterior refresh runs $60K-$150K depending on scope. Doing it wrong destroys the architectural character; doing it right preserves the home.

outline.h2: Why Peninsula Eichlers Have Unique Problems
outline.notes: Explain the construction: post-and-beam framing, exposed structure, radiant slab heating, minimal roof overhangs, T1-11 plywood siding, glass-heavy walls. Every design choice that makes an Eichler an Eichler also makes it uniquely vulnerable. Name the major Eichler tracts: Green Gables, Fairmeadow, Greenmeadow (Palo Alto); Felton Gables, Willows, Vintage Oaks (Menlo Park); Fairglen, Meadows (San Jose); tracts in Foster City and Sunnyvale.

outline.h2: Problem 1: T1-11 Siding Failure
h3: Where and Why T1-11 Fails on Eichlers
Repair Options (Patch, Section Replace, Full Replace)
outline.notes: T1-11 fails at grade (wicking moisture from slab), around windows (aluminum frame water intrusion), and where the plywood delaminates from age. Patch: $500-$1,500 per panel. Section replacement: $4K-$12K. Full T1-11 residing: $28K-$55K. Note that authentic 12-inch groove T1-11 with the right groove depth is increasingly hard to source; most big-box lumber is wrong for Eichlers.

outline.h2: Problem 2: Flat and Low-Slope Roof Failure
h3: Original Built-Up Roofing vs Modern Options
TPO, Modified Bitumen, and PVC Compared
outline.notes: Original Eichler roofs were built-up tar-and-gravel; most have been replaced 1-2 times since. Modern options: TPO ($8-$14/sq ft installed), modified bitumen ($10-$16/sq ft), PVC ($12-$18/sq ft). Full Eichler roof replacement: $25K-$60K depending on size and skylight count. Atrium detailing is a critical Eichler feature that many roofers get wrong — must maintain original scupper and drainage details.

outline.h2: Problem 3: Post-and-Beam Dry Rot at Slab
h3: How to Identify Rot in Load-Bearing Posts
outline.notes: Eichler posts often sit directly on slab with minimal moisture barrier. After 50+ years, base of post rots from the bottom up. Structural — this is not cosmetic. Repair requires temporary shoring, cutting rotted section, replacing with pressure-treated or steel base connector, restoring appearance. Cost: $2K-$5K per post, $15K-$40K for whole-house post remediation. Must be done by licensed contractor with structural engineering sign-off.

outline.h2: Peninsula Permit Reality (By City)
outline.notes: Palo Alto Planning & Development Center — Eichler tracts sometimes have Single-Story Overlay zoning that limits modifications. Menlo Park Community Development — historic district considerations. San Jose Planning, Building & Code Enforcement — most permissive of the Eichler cities. Sunnyvale One-Stop Permit Center — moderate. Foster City — active Eichler preservation neighborhood. Explain that Eichler-specific detail matters for permit approval.

outline.h2: What Contractors Get Wrong on Eichlers
outline.notes: Red flags: switching T1-11 to Hardie or stucco (kills the architecture and often violates neighborhood covenants), installing pitched roof over flat (structural + aesthetic disaster), painting T1-11 with the wrong sheen (Eichlers should have a flat or low-sheen finish), replacing single-pane atrium glass with tinted modern glass (character destroying), skipping the moisture barrier at post bases.

outline.h2: How We Approach Eichler Exterior Work
outline.notes: Our process: full walkthrough with attention to Eichler-specific details, source authentic T1-11 through specialty lumber suppliers, coordinate with structural engineers on any post work, use Eichler-appropriate roofing details (proper scuppers, no ridge caps, atrium detailing preserved), coordinate with local Eichler homeowner associations where applicable.
